devices.label: ISR 4331 branch router
devices.description: Sub-2 Gbps branch services router: 100 Mbps of CEF/IPsec forwarding in the base licence, 300 Mbps with the FL-4330-PERF licence and up to 1.8 Gbps with the booster licence. Three onboard dual-mode GE ports (an RJ-45 and an SFP cage on the same port number, one media active at a time) plus a dedicated GE management port, with two NIM slots, one ISC slot and one SM-X slot for WAN, voice and switching modules.
devices.notes: ISR4331/K9: "3 onboard GE, 2 NIM slots, 1 ISC slot, 1 SM slot". Hardware installation guide, "Dual Mode GE or SFP Ports": the SFP cage shares the physical port with the RJ-45 of the same number and only one media can be active, so each GE port is modelled as a combo pair. GigabitEthernet0 is the separate 10/100/1000 management port. The SFP cages accept 1000BASE-SX/LX/ZX and 100 Mb/s SFPs; PoE+ is not fitted on the 4331 (only 4451-X and 4351 have front-panel PoE+).

devices.label: ASR 1001-X aggregation services router
devices.description: 1 RU 2.5 Gbps - 10 Gbps aggregation router with a fixed ESP and eight built-in Ethernet ports: six 1G SFP-only interfaces and two 10G SFP+ interfaces (10G rate only, SyncE capable). One half-height SPA slot adds further LAN/WAN ports; no copper data ports are fitted, only the 10/100/1000 management port.
devices.notes: ASR 1001-X hardware guide: "Six built-in 1 GE SFP-only interfaces (do not support SFP+), and two built-in 10 GE SFP+ interfaces (support only 10-GE rate)". Nine SPA options exist (1x10GE, 8x1GE, 4x1GE, 1xOC-3, 1xT3/E3, ...) but the SPA slot is empty in the base chassis, so only the fixed ports are modelled. ESP: 2.5 Gbps default, 5/10/20 Gbps with licence.

devices.label: MX204 universal routing platform
devices.description: 1 RU 400 Gbps fixed-configuration edge router: eight 10GE SFP+ ports on PIC 1 plus four rate-selectable QSFP28 ports (PIC 0) that run as 100GE, 40GE, or four 10GE breakouts each, and a single 1G RJ-45 management port. No copper data ports and no line-card slots - the MX204 is fully fixed, with one built-in Routing Engine and 1+1 power supplies.
devices.notes: MX204 chassis documentation: "four rate-selectable ports that can be configured as 100-Gigabit Ethernet ports or 40-Gigabit Ethernet ports, or each port can be configured as four 10-Gigabit Ethernet ports (by using a breakout cable). The MX204 also has eight 10-Gigabit Ethernet ports. The four rate-selectable ports support QSFP28 and QSFP+ transceivers, whereas the eight 10-Gigabit Ethernet ports support SFP+ transceivers." Juniper's port-speed guide splits the router into fixed-port PIC 0 (ports 0-3, 100/40/10G) and MIC PIC 1 (ports 0-7, 10G), which is why the interfaces are et-0/0/0-3 and xe-0/1/0-7. Breakout is one physical cage, so each QSFP28 is a single interface with 40G/100G speed caps.

devices.label: SRX380 SD-WAN security gateway
devices.description: 1 RU branch SD-WAN gateway / firewall rated 20 Gbps firewall and 10 Gbps IMIX routing: 16 PoE-enabled 1G RJ-45 access ports, four MACsec-capable SFP/SFP+ ports that run at 1G or 10G, and a dedicated RJ-45 management port. Four mini-PIM slots take additional WAN or copper/fibre modules.
devices.notes: Juniper HCT hardware specs for SRX380-P-SYS-JB-AC: RJ-45 port count 16, SFP+ port count 4 (both MACsec), management port 1x RJ-45 (fxp0), 4 mini-PIM slots, 2 console ports. The four SFP+ cages accept 1G or 10G optics per the SRX380 chassis documentation ("Four 1 or 10-Gigabit Ethernet MACsec-enabled SFP or SFP+ ports"), hence speedCaps 1000/10000. The 16 copper ports are 802.3at PoE-enabled.

devices.label: 7750 SR-1 service router
devices.description: 1 RU single-slot service router (up to 1.5 Tb/s full duplex on FP4) with one MDA slot fitted with the 6-port QSFP28 MDA-e-XP: six 100GE QSFP28 connectors, each also usable at 40GE or as 10/25GE breakouts. There are no copper data ports and no second line-card slot - capacity and port mix come entirely from the installed MDA.
devices.notes: Nokia 7750 SR data sheet: the SR-1 is a "modular, single-slot system supporting up to 1.5 Tb/s FD" with QSFP56-DD/QSFP28/SFP28 connectors and 10x10GE, 2x100GE and 4x100GE breakout options. The SR OS interface guides use the SR-1 with the 6-port QSFP28 mda-e-xp as the worked example (connector naming slot/mda/connector, i.e. 1/1/c1). Port list shown is that documented build; a different MDA changes the port mix.

devices.label: NetEngine 40E-X8A core router
devices.description: 21 RU core/peering chassis with 51.2 Tbit/s switching capacity and 7232 Mpps forwarding: eight LPU slots (two half-width subslots each), two MPU slots and four SFU slots, shown here fully populated with 32 x 100GE QSFP28 ports (4 per LPU). Line processing units accept E1/POS/CPOS/FE/GE/10GE/40GE/100GE cards, so the port mix follows the installed LPUs.
devices.notes: NE40E-X8A platform table: 51.2 Tbit/s switching, 7232 Mpps, 2 MPU slots, 4 SFU slots, 8 LPU slots, 930 x 442 x 650 mm (21 U), 4770 W max. Huawei's slot map numbers LPUs 1-8 and SRUs 9-10, which is why port names use 100GE<slot>/0/<port>. Interface types supported: E1, POS, CPOS, FE, GE, 10GE, 40GE and 100GE; the 32 x 100GE list is one fully-populated build (8 LPUs x 4 x 100GE), not a fixed port count.

devices.label: 7280R3 48YC8 25G/100G router
devices.description: 1 RU 2 Tbps deep-buffer routing platform with 48 SFP28 ports that run at 1G, 10G or 25G plus 8 QSFP28 ports at 100G or 40G, all fixed - there are no line-card or module slots. Designed for internet peering and WAN edge roles with full BGP tables and a 4 GB buffer.
devices.notes: 7280R3 data sheet: "7280SR3-48YC8 series: 48 port 25G and 8 port 100G", "2 Tbps wire speed performance with 4GB buffer, 48 x 25G SFP and 8 x 100G QSFP". The SFP ports support 1/10/25G operation and the QSFP ports support 100G, 40G or breakout, hence the speedCaps. Fixed 1 RU chassis: no expansion slots.

devices.label: Cloud Core Router CCR2116-12G-4S+
devices.description: 1 RU cloud core router built on a 16-core 2 GHz ARM64 CPU with 16 GB RAM: twelve 1G RJ-45 ports and four 10G SFP+ cages, all wired through the Marvell Aldrin switch chip, plus an M.2 PCIe slot and a serial console. Targets 10G-era BGP and NAT edge roles at a fraction of the cost of a chassis router.
devices.notes: MikroTik product page: "four 10G SFP+ ports ... connected to the Marvell Aldrin family switch chip. Then we have Gigabit Ethernet ports. 12 of them are running through the Marvell chip." Port labels are ether1-ether12 and sfp-sfpplus1-4 as shown in RouterOS. No PoE, no USB data ports (M.2 PCIe slot and 1x RJ-45 serial console only).

devices.label: EdgeRouter Infinity ER-8-XG
devices.description: 1 RU EdgeOS router with an 80 Gbps aggregate forwarding capacity from a 16-core 1.8 GHz CPU and 16 GB DDR4: eight 10G SFP+ cages (eth1-eth8) plus a single 1G RJ-45 port (eth0), with no module slots. Aimed at ISP aggregation and 10G branch uplinks.
devices.notes: Ubiquiti data sheet: "eight 10G SFP+ ports and a Gigabit Ethernet RJ45 port for routing" with 80 Gbps aggregate throughput. The ER-8-XG quick start guide labels the front panel "SFP+ (eth1-eth8)" for the hot-swappable 10G cages and "RJ45 (eth0)" for the 10/100/1000 port, so the copper port is eth0, not eth8. An RJ-45 serial console sits alongside but is not a data port.

devices.label: vSRX virtual firewall (SD-WAN edge)
devices.description: Virtual Junos firewall/router instance for branch and SD-WAN edges: up to 10 vNICs, with fxp0 reserved for out-of-band management and ge-0/0/0 upward mapped to traffic vNICs at the hypervisor's NIC speed. There is no physical hardware - port count follows the vNIC set attached to the VM.
devices.notes: vSRX on VMware specification table: "vNICs: Up to 10 vNICs (SR-IOV)"; interface mapping is fxp0 for out-of-band management and ge-0/0/0 for the first traffic vNIC. Cloud variants are smaller (AWS and GCP cap at 8 interfaces, Nutanix 8). Modelled with 10 vNICs at 1G because the link rate is whatever the hypervisor NIC provides, not a fixed optic.

devices.label: FortiGate 100F secure SD-WAN gateway
devices.description: 1 RU secure SD-WAN appliance with 20 Gbps firewall and 11.5 Gbps IPsec throughput on the purpose-built SD-WAN ASIC: 18 x 1G RJ-45 ports (MGMT/DMZ, WAN1-WAN2, HA1-HA2 and port1-12), four 1G SFP cages (13-16), four RJ-45/SFP shared pairs (17-20) where only one half of each pair can be used, and two 10G SFP+ FortiLink ports (X1-X2). No expansion slots.
devices.notes: FortiGate 100F/101F fast-path architecture doc: "Two 10/100/1000BASE-T Copper (DMZ, MGMT). Sixteen 10/100/1000BASE-T Copper (WAN1, WAN2, HA1, HA2, 1 to 12). Two 10 GigE SFP+ (X1 and X2) ... Four 1GigE SFP (13 to 16). Four shared interfaces (17 to 20) that can be either 10/100/1000BASE-T Copper or 1GE SFP." Ports 17-20 are therefore modelled as combo pairs: "there are two sets of physical interfaces numbered 17 to 20 but only one of each can be connected to a network". Interface names follow FortiOS (port1-port20, wan1/wan2, ha1/ha2, dmz, mgmt, x1/x2) with the SFP half of a shared pair suffixed -sfp because FortiOS gives both halves the same name.

devices.label: FortiGate 200F secure SD-WAN gateway
devices.description: 1 RU campus/enterprise-branch secure SD-WAN gateway at 27 Gbps firewall and 13 Gbps IPsec: 16 x 1G RJ-45 switch ports, 8 x 1G SFP cages (17-24), 4 x 10G SFP+ ports (X1-X2 network, X3-X4 FortiLink) and dedicated MGMT and HA RJ-45 ports. Fixed chassis, no expansion slots.
devices.notes: FortiGate 200F data sheet: "18 x GE RJ45 (including 1 x MGMT port, 1 x HA port, 16 x switch ports), 8 x GE SFP slots, 2 x 10GE SFP+ slots, 2 x 10GE SFP+ FortiLink slots". Front panel callouts: 2x GE RJ45 HA/MGMT, 16x GE RJ45, 2x 10GE SFP+ (X1-X2), 2x 10GE SFP+ FortiLink (X3-X4), 8x GE SFP. No shared media pairs on this model, unlike the 100F.
